title: MIT Energy Initiative conference explores energy transition and AI power demands
excerpt: Experts discussed the energy requirements of data centers and strategies for carbon mitigation at the September 22-23 conference.
bodyHtml:
The MIT Energy Initiative held its annual research conference on September 22-23, 2026, to explore the energy transition. The event featured discussions on the rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence and the energy requirements for data centers, alongside research on carbon utilization and nuclear power.

Steve Clemmer of the Union of Concerned Scientists stated that new hyperscale facilities built for artificial intelligence can use more power than entire cities. He noted that increased reliance on fossil fuels will result in tens of billions of dollars in health damages, and trillions in climate damages.

Larry Susskind of the MIT Department of Urban Studies and Planning recommended that developers engage in facilitated negotiations with local groups to establish community benefits agreements. He stated that developers must accept that they cannot rush community acceptance and that they have to proceed at the speed of trust.
topic: Powering up for a pivotal moment
